findings: Retain the accurate structure of the migration and both modes, date it to April, add the November base as navigation, and qualify the existing PaymentMethod migration starting point. Source lines 55–79 should cover both Intent types, separate endpoint action and outcome, and include the server-confirm sample's client-secret handoff for remaining client actions.

Source lines 13–24 summarize the April feature table too broadly. Preserve automatic carriage of collected/configured context in the dated mobile workflow. Token shipping, mandate data, return URL and `setup_future_usage` are nullable, and saving via future-use configuration requires the PaymentIntent Customer when the described automatic attachment occurs, confirmation, and completion of any required actions (`raw/stripe-api-confirmation-tokens-object-2026-11-07.md:89-128`; old raw lines 8-22,59-103). The guide's server-side CVC capability compares its two migration paths. The related April 22 mobile guide requires payment-details collection before creating an Intent, optional SDK CVC configuration and server-side Customer or customer Account plus the card option `require_cvc_recollection` (`raw/stripe-inapp-finalize-payments-server-2025.md:774-819,846-862`). Do not present it as automatic, mandatory, or an SDK/platform-independent CVC guarantee.

The April guide and summary support both client and server initial confirmation for PaymentIntent or SetupIntent (old raw lines 51-103,128-180,219-271; source lines 55–79). The samples create PaymentIntents, while the related November SetupIntent reference confirms its distinct endpoint and optional `confirmation_token` parameter. Directly provided corresponding Intent fields take precedence at confirmation for both objects (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:412-427`, `raw/stripe-api-setup-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:367-376`). Preserve the client-secret response in the server-confirm example and show that the app may still perform required next actions; server confirmation is an attempt and client-secret return does not prove payment or completed setup (`raw/stripe-inapp-finalize-payments-server-2025.md:309-315,425-437`, `raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-confirm-2026-11-07.md:5-17`). Add this scope to the mapped source and reciprocal in-app routes.

The April React Native block expects `clientSecret` and supplies 6099 in IntentConfiguration, while the shared sample server returns `client_secret` and hardcodes 1099 (old raw lines 188-217,229-241,250-264). These examples are sketches and must not be copied together without normalizing the merchant JSON contract and matching the client/server Intent configuration. The April iOS snippet also invokes an unspecified `intentCreationCallback` inside a continuation without showing a resume (old raw lines 34-49), while the separately retained April finalize guide shows an async callback returning the server's client-secret string or throwing (`raw/stripe-inapp-finalize-payments-server-2025.md:309-337`). Document the verified flow and qualify the raw snippets rather than implying a runnable sample.

The scoped retained SDK snapshots support the token path without a universal removal of the legacy path. React Native 0.84.0 `2026-10-29-33ef1ee` retains both alternative handler options, requires exactly one for a deferred Intent without a client secret, documents matching IntentConfiguration and maps token callback result to a client-secret string or error (`package.json:1-10`, `src/types/PaymentSheet.ts:585-629`, `src/functions.ts:363-386`, `ios/StripeSdkImpl+PaymentSheet.swift:217-245`). Android 23.25.1 `2026-10-27-bb0d8d0` retains mutually exclusive legacy and ConfirmationToken `createIntentCallback` overloads (`gradle.properties:25-27`, `PaymentSheet.kt:421-442`). iOS 26.11.0 `2026-09-30-7037819` retains branches for both configured handlers and defines `STPConfirmationToken.stripeId` and optional `paymentMethodPreview` (`StripePaymentSheet.podspec:1-9`, `PaymentSheet+DeferredAPI.swift:12-59`, `STPConfirmationToken.swift:10-48`). Keep the April callback advice dated and SDK-specific. These signatures are separate evidence from the November navigation capture.

The April examples explicitly enable automatic payment methods (old raw lines 63-73,84-96). The separately retained 2026-07-29.dahlia changelog says `allowed_payment_method_types` is mutually exclusive with `automatic_payment_methods` and other controls (`raw/stripe-changelog-dahlia-2026-07-29-allowed-payment-method-types-parameter-2026-11-07.md:7-13`), so avoid combining the dated examples' setting with that alternative when using that versioned request path.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-mobile-migration-confirmation-tokens-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-inapp-migrate-confirmation-tokens-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-migrate-confirmation-tokens.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/migration-confirmation-tokens`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/migration-confirmation-tokens states the migration goal of using a ConfirmationToken in place of a PaymentMethod and routes iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-15). The 2026-04-23 guide assumes an existing mobile PaymentMethod integration and points new builds to the separate accept-payment guide (old raw lines 8-26). Mobile PaymentSheet uses a token callback and its token ID for the server path, with SDK-specific callback interfaces (old raw lines 32-49, old raw lines 109-126 and old raw lines 186-217). In client-side confirmation the server creates an unconfirmed PaymentIntent or SetupIntent and the app uses its client secret to confirm through the SDK with the token. In server-side confirmation the app sends the token ID and the server creates and attempts to confirm the Intent with `confirmation_token` and `confirm: true`; the sample returns the Intent's client secret. Explicit corresponding Intent fields at confirmation override token values (old raw lines 51-103 and old raw lines 219-273). The preview is payment-method information, and token generation, Intent creation and a returned client secret are separate from completion. The related April server guide says the app can still finish next actions after server confirmation (`raw/stripe-inapp-finalize-payments-server-2025.md:309-315`). source-stripe-inapp-migrate-confirmation-tokens.md retains the two modes but its abbreviated server flow omits the client-secret handoff and distinct SetupIntent endpoint, and its automatic-context and CVC wording needs scope.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/migration-confirmation-tokens, November changed the base presentation to three links for the same platforms (new raw lines 9-15). Retain April's dated prerequisite, UI callback paths, two confirmation modes and override rule (old raw lines 24-49 and old raw lines 51-103). source-stripe-inapp-migrate-confirmation-tokens.md and the in-app concept should qualify automatic carriage as use of collected or configured fields. For example, `setup_future_usage` can be null and the described automatic attachment needs a Customer, confirmed PaymentIntent and completed actions. Server-side saved-card CVC re-collection is an optional configured feature with client collection and a server card option (`raw/stripe-api-confirmation-tokens-object-2026-11-07.md:89-128`, `raw/stripe-inapp-finalize-payments-server-2025.md:774-819`). Keep server confirmation distinct from client next actions and from successful payment or setup (`raw/stripe-inapp-finalize-payments-server-2025.md:309-315,425-437`).
